author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that he discussed the release of political prisoners in China with his counterpart, Xi Jinping, in Washington last week.
“We talked, and I think we had some very, very important discussions. Hopefully fruitful discussions,” Trump told reporters in the White House.
Families had stepped up pressure on the Trump administration to push Beijing to release their loved ones ahead of Xi’s three-day state visit.
In the lead-up to the summit, the White House...
title: Trump claims he discussed release of political prisoners in China with Xi at summit

author: Han Li
description:
At a hearing reviewing China’s compliance with its World Trade Organization (WTO) commitments, a senior US trade official said Beijing was targeting entire industrial sectors for global dominance while retaining a non-market economic system.
Terry McCartin, Assistant US Trade Representative (USTR) for China, Mongolia and Taiwan Affairs, said China’s anticompetitive behaviour posed a major challenge to the global trading system.
“More critically, after 25 years of WTO membership, China still...
title: US criticises China’s WTO compliance as industry groups mount complaints

author: Xinlu Liang
description:
The fields in Xinjiang’s Awati county – a cotton hub hit by US sanctions – were nearly ready for the October harvest.
Yusup Molamaiti, a 36-year-old technician, recalled what it was like manually planting and harvesting 37 mu (about 2.5 hectares or 6 acres) of scattered plots of land.
“Planting a single mu took up to three hours with two people laying plastic film by hand,” he said. Harvesting would lock his family into year-round labour, yielding just 250-300kg (551-661lbs) per mu.
Today, his...
title: US sanctions forced Xinjiang cotton to adapt, but survival comes at a cost

author: Nayan Seth
description:
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Wednesday proposed a new global framework to tackle excess steel production capacity on the sidelines of the ongoing Group of 20 Trade Ministers’ meeting, just days after Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to the United States.
“The United States has taken robust measures, and it probably makes sense for other countries to do that too,” Greer said after a meeting of the Global Forum on Steel Excess Capacity (GFSEC) in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.
“Well,...
title: US targets China’s steel capacity at G20 days after Xi’s state visit

author: Igor Patrick
description:
China will charge an extra 55 per cent tariff on Brazilian beef from Thursday after Brazil filled its import quota for the year and has not agreed to let Brazilian exporters use the unfilled quota of neighbouring Uruguay, industry sources said.
The Chinese Ministry of Commerce announced the surtax on Wednesday, a day after China’s customs administration confirmed that Brazil had used all of its 1.106 million-tonne allowance for 2026, and under the rules the extra tariff applies from the third...
title: China slaps 55% tariff on Brazilian beef, rebuffs bid to borrow Uruguay’s quota

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
A decades-long effort by Beijing and Washington to recover the remains of US servicemen missing in China since World War II has resurfaced in the wake of the summit between the nations’ leaders.
The commitment was included in an eight-point list of outcomes from Chinese President Xi Jinping’s three-day state visit last week, alongside other agreements covering issues including artificial intelligence and trade.
According to a statement issued by China’s foreign ministry after the summit, the two...
title: Why did Trump and Xi seal a deal on World War II soldiers’ missing remains?

author: William Zheng,Alyssa Chen
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping projected a message of confidence about the country’s ability to overcome challenges during his annual National Day address, issuing a rallying call for robust economic growth and more certainty amid geopolitical complications.
Xi’s address, delivered at a state reception in Beijing on Wednesday evening to mark the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic, was his first to the nation following his state visit to the US last week. It came weeks ahead...
title: Xi projects confidence in National Day speech, with rallying call for economic growth

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together stories from our coverage of the Xi-Trump summit. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Why Xi Jinping skipped the UN after his Trump summit

Han Zheng, China’s vice-president, called on “major countries” to respect the sovereignty and security of Middle Eastern nations and bring about a two-state solution for the “Palestinian question” on Saturday at the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in an implicit dig at the US and Israel.
2. ‘Right...
title: From Taiwan to Takaichi, the geopolitical fallout from Xi-Trump summit

author: David Gorombolyi
description:
We are reminded seemingly daily of the great power transitions that ended in conflict. However, it is the exceptions – the ones that did not result in war – that could have real lessons to offer.
Today, the question is more than academic. Standing beside US President Donald Trump at the White House last week, President Xi Jinping proposed that competition between China and the United States should be “a race of catching up with one another”, not “a wrestle where one either wins or...
title: US-China conflict doesn’t have to become a self-fulfilling prophecy

author: Amber Wang
description:
Disagreement over how to prevent conflicts could explain why Chinese and US accounts characterised discussions at last week’s summit so differently, analysts said.
Speaking at a White House arrival ceremony, Chinese President Xi Jinping said the two militaries should maintain regular dialogue and “improve mechanisms for crisis communication and prevention”.
In a statement issued after the summit, China’s foreign ministry said the countries’ militaries had agreed “to conclude a memorandum of...
title: Did Beijing and Washington agree on a crisis prevention deal, or not?

author: Chao Kong
description:
A computer simulation developed by Chinese researchers suggests that a missile-borne system with the latest light detection and ranging system, or lidar, could detect and track an F-35 stealth fighter at up to 61.5km (38 miles) at night.
The theoretical model developed by a leading Chinese air force missile supplier says that under ideal conditions, the claimed range could have implications for the F-35’s ability to survive while facing China’s stealth fighters.
But one analyst is sceptical that...
title: Chinese researchers say missile lidar model can spot US F-35 at up to 61.5km

author: Holly Chik
description:
Scientists have unveiled an exceptionally well-preserved 100-million-year-old fossil of a small, feathered dinosaur in northeastern China that could reshape our understanding of how dinosaurs took to the skies.
The newly discovered species, named Norellraptor barsboldi, is a four-winged predatory dinosaur measuring 57cm (22 inches) long.
Belonging to the microraptorines – small dinosaurs with feathers and wings closely related to birds – the creature offers fresh evidence that flight evolved...
title: 4-winged fossil found in Liaoning challenges single origin of dinosaur flight

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
Brussels and Berlin are steeling themselves for a make-or-break October with China, as the mood towards Beijing hardens in both capitals.
The month ahead could help set the course of the increasingly thorny EU-China relationship for years to come, as Europe gears up to present a slew of new tools for countering Beijing’s trade practices, likely to come in December.
Before then, EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic travels to Beijing on October 8 and 9 for crucial meetings with Chinese Commerce Minister...
title: EU weighs sweeping new trade powers against China before make-or-break October

author: Meredith Chen
description:
China’s broadcasting regulator has called for greater support for live-action dramas as the government seeks to steer the booming microdrama industry towards higher-quality production and tighter rights safeguards amid the rapid rise of AI.
Artificial intelligence (AI) has created innovation and production possibilities for microdramas, while also posing challenges over content quality and rights protection, according to Wang Xiaoliang from the National Radio and Television...
title: Slow is beautiful: China launches war against AI drama, goes beyond algorithms

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan’s military plans to spend more than NT$27 billion (US$850 million) to quadruple critical ammunition stocks to 120 days’ supply, strengthening its ability to sustain combat operations during a wartime blockade.
The proposed six-year “urgent ammunition replenishment” programme, running from this year until 2031, comes as Taipei seeks to strengthen its ability to keep fighting if a cross-strait conflict cuts external supply lines.
The spending proposal was revealed on September 26 and still...
title: Taiwan plans US$850 million ammunition spend to prepare for potential PLA blockade

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
The two-month extension of the US-China trade truce remains fragile despite last week’s summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, with modest economic concessions leaving deeper disputes unresolved, Asia Society Policy Institute analysts said on Tuesday.
“In my view, this truce is very fragile,” said Wendy Cutler, an Asia Society Policy Institute vice-president and former acting deputy US trade representative. “I think they’re testing each other.”
Xi’s three-day state visit to...
title: US-China trade truce remains ‘fragile’ after Xi-Trump summit, analysts say

author: Han Li
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping’s three-day state visit to Washington is over, but China watchers in Congress and the US-China policy community are still parsing a wide range of outcomes, with two more leadership summits expected before the end of the year.
The talks between Xi and US President Donald Trump produced a series of joint announcements, including an extension of the US-China trade truce, investment commitments, an agreement to continue an AI dialogue and high-level engagement, as well...
title: ‘Hold the status quo’? US Congress reviews Xi-Trump summit outcomes
